body_en_plain:
M O R E   M A I L ! !

  February, 1992     Page Reply

 Ken Stearn...........02    08

 Alan D. Cox..........17    21

 Stuart Burton........22    26

 Colin Macdonald......30    32

 Tim Wells............34    35

 Jon Harry............36    38

 David Wornham........40    45

From: Ken Stearn, FIFE


Dear Outlet,

I have just received 'OUTWRITE'
and,as expected, it is a quality
piece of work. I have bought
'OUTLET' from the start so am
well accustomed to this standard
of software. My compliments to
Bob Wilkinson.

I recently took a look at some
of the other SAM magazines on
offer and can assure you that
'OUTLET' still reigns supreme.
One mag. was even threatening
violence to another mag!! Who
says computer games don't breed
violence?

I'd like to have the following
piece of "Japanese Gaelic" (!)
translated into English so I
can use downloaded fonts on my
24-pin Toshiba printer (Epson-
compatible) connected to SAM's
communication interface. I have
typed out the relevant passage
from the manual...

       SELECT USER
ESC %  DEFINED CHARACTER SET

Function: Selects the character
          set you specify

Sequence    ESC %

Hex.        1B 25 n

Dec.        27 37 n

Discussion  The value of n is a
            binary number that
            identifies either a
            resident character
            set or a down-loaded
            one.

00H (0 decimal) Specifies a
                resident set

01H (1 decimal) Specifies a
                downloaded set

The printer ignores this command
if the font is not loaded.

ESC &   SPECIFY USER DEFINED
        CHARACTERS

Function:Specifies user
         designed character sets

Sequence:ESC & 00 n1 n2 [d1 d2
         d3 data...] n2-n1+1

Hex      1B 26 00 n1 n2 [d1 d2
         d3 data...] n2-n1+1

DEC      27 38 0  n1 n2 [d1 d2
         d3 data...] n2-n1+1


Discussion: All parameters are
binary numbers. n1 and n2
identify the start and end codes
to be defined.

d1 sets the amount of space you
want to add to the left of the
character, d2 the pattern width
and d3 sets the space to the
right. The parameters d1 d2 d3
must satisfy these conditions:-

            d2          d1+d2+d3
  Mode  (max.value)  (max.value)
  ----  -----------  -----------

Draft mode    9          12
LQ mode at
10 cpi       29          36

LQ mode at
12 cpi       23          30

LQ mode at
15 cpi       15          24

Proportional
pitch        38          42

The data defines the character
pattern. In normal mode, each
character requires three bytes
of data (d2*3).

A dot column represents three
data bytes in normal mode and
two data bytes in superscript/
subscript mode. The msb of the
first byte corresponds to the
top pin of the column,while the
lsb of the third byte (in normal
mode) corresponds to the bottom
pin. Each character with a code
between n1 and n2 must be
defined. This means that...

d2*3*(n2-n1+1) or d2*3*(n2-n1+1)
data bytes are required.

I have tried to load both 8-bit
and 16-bit fonts to no avail.
But of course I am at a loss as
to how to enter them. I hope you
can help.
                    Ken Stearn

Brian Cavers to Ken Stearn

In BASIC, you use the LPRINT
command to send data to your
printer and each piece of data
is a number between 0 and 255.
However, the SAM Coupe and most
Spectrum printer interfaces have
two"modes" of sending this data:
as pure code or in "expanded"
form. In this expanded form many
of the codes are stopped by the
computer and instead, a keyword
is sent. This is for printing a
BASIC listing etc. To switch the
printer to do things like BOLD
printing or ITALICS you need to
send "control" codes. To do this
you need first to make sure your
computer is in the "pure code"
mode as follows...

To send control codes, first:

OPEN #3;"B"          SAM COUPE,
                     OPUS,MDRIVE

POKE @6,1            DISCIPLE/+D

FORMAT LPRINT "U"    +3

COPY: REM CHR$ 0     KEMPSTON E

After, use LPRINT to send codes.
For example, to send code 65 you
LPRINT CHR$ 65. Codes between 32
and 127 also have an "ASCII"
equivalent so you can use that
instead if you know it. To find
it just enter,e.g.,PRINT CHR$ 65
and you will see a capital A on
your computer screen so you can
use LPRINT "A" instead of the
LPRINT CHR$ 65 if you want!

I mention that because you may
wonder what the printer manual
means when it's got ESC &. This
means the code for ESC (which is
27) and "&" (code 38) so that
could be sent to the printer
with either...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 38;  or...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;"&";

           ...it means the same.
If you enter PRINT CHR$ 38 you
will see a "&" on your screen.If
you enter PRINT CODE "&" you
will see 38 printed on your
screen.Get it? Under the heading
ESC & in your list next to DEC
you will see it starts 27 38 0
plus other things so enter...

10 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"&";CHR$ 0;
  (tells printer,font is coming)

20 LPRINT CHR$ 32;
   (first character. - the SPACE
   character. This is n1 in your
   list)

30 LPRINT CHR$ 127;
  (last character, the copyright
  sign. This is n2 in your list)

40 LPRINT CHR$ 0;
          (left gap width before
          character. This is d1)

50 LPRINT CHR$ 16;
   (character pattern width. d2)

60 LPRINT CHR$ 4;
           (right gap width. d3)

You can try different numbers in
lines 40 to 60 but they must not
exceed the max values in your
list. You may need to experiment
and I am assuming the fonts you
have are 16 dots wide (line 50)
so you may need to adjust that.
They could be 8 or 24 dots wide
for all I know! Send me one of
your fonts if you have trouble
here so I can examine it.

Make sure you include all the
semi-colons (;) in the above as
I think you may get a linefeed
when you don't want one!

Following the above,your printer
should be awaiting the actual
font data ("data" in your list)
and this is done thus...

You must first load the font in
your computer's memory. Any free
area will do but let's use say,
32768. To load it and send it to
your printer you need to know
the length of the font code. On
SAM, Disciple and +D you can get
this using DIR 1. The length is
the number on the far right of
the filename. Other users will
need a header reader if they do
not know the length. Suppose the
length is'L'.Add to the program:

70 LOAD "FONTNAME" CODE 32768

80 LPRINT MEM$(32768 TO 32767+L)
                         (SAM)
or...
   FOR N=32768 TO 32767+L:
   LPRINT CHR$ PEEK N; : NEXT N
                      (Spectrum)

Obviously, you can add 32767 to
the length and put the sum where
I have put 32767+L.

A 24-bit font is needed so I
just don't know if the fonts you
have are suitable. Let me know.

Next you must add the number of
characters which is 96. This is
the bit at the end which says:
n2-n1+1 and you get it from 127
(the final character in the font
- the copyright sign) MINUS 32
(the SPACE character) PLUS 1. If
you only send a few characters
you must change that along with
the numbers in lines 20 and 30.

Finally, SAVE the program so you
can use it again or change it if
there's an error!

Having SAVEd it you can now RUN
the program and the font should
download. When you want to use
the new font you must use...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;"%";CHR$ 1;

Thereafter anything you print
should use the new font so you
could add a test line to the
program...

110 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"%";CHR$ 1;

120 CLOSE #3: OPEN #3;"T"
      (+3 use FORMAT LPRINT "E",
       +D use POKE @6,0)

130 LPRINT "MESSAGE..."

Line 120 is to end sending codes
ready to send ordinary text.

To switch back to the printer's
own font you need to use...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;"%";CHR$ 0;

           ...but remember, you
MUST always use OPEN #3;"B"
before sending codes (unless you
have previously opened it).

If you have problems please let
me know and preferably send me a
copy of your font on disc and
any print-out you may have done.

I regret I don't have a 24-pin
printer so can't test this so if
anyone else spots a fault or,
indeed can give us info on how
to download 24-bit fonts, please
let us all know!
                        - Brian

From: Alan Cox, DYFED

Regarding the 'reverse listing'
bug, as I pointed out earlier, I
have been in correspondence with
Andy Wright and he agrees there
is a bug in SAM BASIC (which he
has cured in Master BASIC). He
has agreed that although it will
embarrass him (although I can't
think why - I could not write
any version of BASIC, let alone
one as useful as his!) I can
write to you describing the
cause of the problem and the way
to get around it in SAM BASIC.

The original problem has been
discussed in various earlier
letters, and in mine of 8
December I set down a way to


create the problem on what a
thought was a regular basis, but
clearly I was wrong, since you
cannot reproduce it, nor can I
always (but no, I do not use
data REMs or line 0).

When I wrote to Andy he
originally suggested that the
problem was due to the use of
indented listings - and I think
the best thing is to reproduce
exactly what he said to me:

"I think I have already found
and fixed the bug you mention (a
ROM BUG) with an MBAS patch. If
you were using an indented
listing, and the initial listing
made a line take up X screen
lines, and it was scrolled just

off the screen top and you up-
arrowed and the new less-indent-
ed form of the line that would
appear took up X-1 lines, the
ROM tried to LDIR 0 bytes of a
table and actually did 65536..."

In a subsequent letter in
response to mine pointing out I
was not using indented listings
he says that the actual bug I
was getting - I sent a disk with
a particular program on it that
always misbehaved - was another
version of the one he described.

He also commented that the
problem should never occur if
you press RETURN, or CLS, before
LISTing, and I now try to do
this as a regular thing.

I note your comments on the
SWIFT 24e in the current OUTLET.
When I finally bought myself a
'real' printer to supplement my
HR5 I opted for the SWIFT 24,
and was delighted when what I
actually got was a 24e. I can
confirm the increased speed,
quoted as 216 cps, as against
192 for the older model: in
addition there are now 6 built-
in fonts (not all that marvel-
lous, but entirely adequate for
my needs), and the control panel
works in 5 different languages.

I bought from Silica Systems,
who regularly advertise, who
give an excellent and fast
service and who were still, at
least up to the end of December,
providing the free colour kit.

Citizen have also introduced a
224 model, which looks a lot
like the old SWIFT 24 in
performance: Silica Systems are
currently advertising this at
`199.00 + VAT.

         All best wishes

           Alan D.Cox






Many thanks for all the feedback
and info, Alan.

                        - Brian

From: Stuart Burton, POOLE

Dear Brian,

I wrote some 48K Spectrum BASIC
programs which are on microdrive
and would like to transfer them
to SAM. I do not have a reliable
tape player. Any suggestions
please? Do any keywords besides
SAVE and VERIFY need to be
retyped? (My programs take up
47.999K!)

I was most surprised to read
Alan Cox's reply to my letter in
OUTLET 52 as I confess I had
omitted to read the OUTLETTERS
and was unaware that you had
included my comment on reverse
listing problems.

You asked if there was anything
odd about the programs in which
it resets. The program is my own
and is all BASIC and is over
300K with a lot of arrays - some
of which are three-dimensional.


The listing runs to thousands of
lines. The effect is only rare
even with long listings but
there is one variation which
seems constant and that occurs
when attempting to scroll up
past a line which is over one
screen long (such as line 8131
in my program "Invotek"). The
computer "locks up" at the
offending line and will usually
not respond to ESC.

I've sent a copy of the program
but would be grateful if you
would NOT publish it as it is
used in my business and contains
confidential information.

Incidentally, I use the program
to prepare price lists and
automatically calculate the
prices of assemblies of
components. It is also used to
estimate the components needed
for a job and in five minutes
does calculations that used to
take over a week to do manually.

By including customers' names
and addresses it is used for
quotations and order acknow-
ledgements. It allows multiple
layers (assemblies of

assemblies) and permits 2500
components and up to 2000
assemblies.

A search facility permits the
recipe for a part to be easily
found.

        Yours sincerely,

          Stuart Burton

Brian Cavers to Stuart Burton

I made a temporary copy of your
program because our 512K SAM is
out of order. However, the fact
that it is so huge is clearly
relevant. You might try adding a
non-functioning new line near
the start just to move BASIC...

 5 IF 1=2 THEN PRINT 9,9,9,9,9

Don't use a REM because it will
use less memory.Try adding more
and more 9's if it does not work
immediately. It often cures
paging problems that I get.

It's good to see a SAM program
being used so effectively in a
genuine business application.

I would say it will be virtually
impossible to move microdrive
programs to SAM without a tape
recorder because the only other
way is by the Messenger and this
may well clash with Interface 1
(Does anyone know?).

In your place I would either try
to borrow a tape recorder from a
friend or try adjusting and
cleaning your present one(unless
you know for certain that there
is some other fault).

To clean it, get a tape head
cleaning pack from any hi-fi
shop. This will have a bottle of
spirit and some means to apply
it to the head. I actually just
use a tissue these days if I can
get a finger in!

To adjust the recording head you
need a very fine screwdriver and
this only works with those tape
recorders that have a tiny hole
to one side of the casing on top
near where the recording head is
located.


Put a music cassette in the tape
recorder and play it. Poke the
sharp end of the screwdriver in
the tiny hole! Fiddle around
until you feel it has located in
the tiny screw therein. Now,turn
it clockwise half a turn and
then again, listening to the
sound of the music. Now turn it
back two half-turns so you are
back where you started. Do the
same anti-clockwise.

You should have heard the music
become muffled as you turned but
become much sharper and clearer
at a certain position so leave
it at that position (unless it's
a Des O'Connor album in which
case I'd leave it muffled and
forget your microdrive programs,
it's not worth it).

Sorry, that's the best I can do
unless anyone else would like to
volunteer to transfer your pro-
grams (assuming there's only two
or three).

If you get them on tape then use
the "BASIC TRANSLATOR" option on
the MGT disc to load them in
SAM. NO keywords need changing
but microdrive syntax will, of
course.                 - Brian

From: Colin Macdonald, FRED mag.



Dear Brian and Ron,

Thanks for the recent issue of
OUTLET. There are, however, a
few things I feel I should point
out. 'POPCORN' by Mike Andrews
(AJ) first appeared in FRED 15,
screen cruncher by D. Gommeren
first appeared in FRED 14, the
IQ-Test by "Alfa Soft" first
appeared in FRED 10, the clip-
art by Leif Mortensen has been
available through his magazine
for about 12 months now and
three of the pictures in Demopix
have appeared on various PD
discs.

Sorry to be the bringer of bad
news if you didn't already know,
however, hopefully as many
OUTLET readers are "techies",
they won't have subscribed to
FRED etc.

          Best wishes,

         Colin Macdonald

Brian Cavers to Colin Macdonald

Thanks,Colin. This letter raises
an interesting point - that of
material appearing in more than
one disc magazine and I thought
it worth airing in public.

I don't mind really if another
magazine beats us to it with a
particular item. OUTLET makes no
claim that its contents have
never been published before but
simply tries to provide an
outlet for the average user to
share software. I know that many
who write software at home want
only that it be spread around as
much as possible and in that
same spirit I'm happy that as
many people as possible get to
use such programs.

It is inevitable that different
magazines publishing material
from the public will contain
common items...

"POPCORN" is the property of its
author, Mike Andrews,who sent it
to us months ago. "SCRUNCH",
"IQ-TEST" and much of our clip
art are from Leif Mortensen. The
high-res screens are public
domain and mostly ported across
from the ST, Amiga and PC - some
of it is years old and available
from PD libraries long before
SAM even existed. For instance,
the "diamond ring" screen in the
latest FRED was in OUTLET 39 in
November, 1990! (I got it off an
ST disc). No, I don't regard it
as "bad news" but only to be
expected.              - Brian.

From: Tim Wells, LEEDS

Dear Sir,

I require one of those rare dev-
ices -an MGT Twoface to transfer
programs between Spectrum and
SAM because my Messenger clashes
with the disk system I use - an
OPUS SPECTRADOS interface with
dual 3-inch drives (which no-one
else has heard of - have you any
knowledge about this?).

I am willing to pay a reasonable
price for the Twoface or hire
one if necessary. Do any of your
readers know where I can get
one?
        Yours faithfully,
            Tim Wells

Brian Cavers to Tim Wells

Yes, Brian Gaff tells me he used
to have a Spectrados interface.
It was the forerunner of the
Opus Discovery but used separate
drives. Brian also has a Twoface
and says you can borrow it to
try if you write to him (see BG
Services address in OUTBOARD)
and pay the postage.

However, note that you cannot be
sure that it will do the job as
the Twoface doesn't solve all
interfacing problems. You may
finish up having to save to tape
and then reload!

                        - Brian

From: Jon Harry, RUISLIP

Dear Sirs,

  Re: OUTWRITE! WORD PROCESSOR

I am currently running OUTWRITE!
on my Sam Coupe, and may I say
that I find it very user-
friendly once the various
command keys have been learned.

However, I am suspicious that
there may be a minor programming
error present, and am seeking
your advice.

When using OUTWRITE! to print on
standard A4 paper, it is first
necessary to enter 'EDIT Z' to
reset the printer configuration.

After having done this you have
the option to SAVE to disk,
using 'wordcd', start address
65536, length 16384. However, I
suspect that the segment really
required is 'wordcd2', as this
appears when requesting a disk
directory. The segment 'wordcd'
has no effect whatsoever on the
package as each time I reload
OUTWRITE!, I have to re-set the
printer defaults, and the
additional (non-functional)
segment 'wordcd' appears on the
disk directory.

I would be grateful if you could
confirm my findings, and advise
me if there is any (known) way
round it.
                 Jon Harry

Brian Cavers to Jon Harry



I'm sorry about the problem with
OUTWRITE! We were not aware of
this bug - presumably because
there is a main "RESAVE PROGRAM"
option in the main menu which
probably most people may have
used initially when customising.


This is, in fact, one answer to
the problem - after making your
changes at the printer menu, say
"N" at the prompt "resave code?"
but then go back to the main
menu and select the option to
save a working copy; this
includes a save of the code.

Alternatively, to correct the
BASIC properly, you can just
alter the SAVE "wordcd" in line
1150 to SAVE "wordcd2" but to
make this a permanent change of
the BASIC you still need to use
the "save a working copy" at the
main menu.

Once again, I'm sorry for any
inconvenience this has caused
but thank you for drawing my
attention to it.

                      - Brian

       Flexibase Software
       -------------------
        tel.(0905) 775840
David Wornham. 20 The Parklands,
Droitwich Spa, Worcs. WR9 7DG
--------------------------------

Dear Brian and Ron,

     OUTWRITE & STYLE WRITER

Thank  you  for sending me the
copy of Outwrite and Style
Writer as  ordered. I have yet
to try Style Writer which was
purchased for its graphics
inclusion capability but am now
using Outwrite in  preference
to Sam Tasword and am impressed
with its speed, screen  style
and keyboard feel.

Outwrite performs well with my
"nearly-Epson-compatible" Shinwa
printer but the enlarged (width)
printing code needs changing. I
forward the following suggest-
ions for minor improvements:


a)  Optional  DIR?  on  Load
and  Save.  I have amended this
by amending  Lines  280  and
370 to:

CLS:PRINT "Dir?":POKE SVAR 618,0
:BEEP .1,40:BEEP .2,36 :PAUSE 0:
IF INKEY$="d" (or "y" if
preferred) THEN DIR PEEK 23047


b) As requested by others, left
and right margins.

   SOUND MACHINE AND FLEXIPAGE


Having purchased a copy of Sound
Machine from the Sam stand at
the December London show, I have
completed working my way through
the manual and can say that I'M
VERY IMPRESSED at its profess-
ional looks, feel,capability and
general usefulness. It's ideal
for non- musical persons to
learn about music writing and
for those already having musical
knowledge to use Sam's excellent
6-channel sound chip with ease.

Melodies can be composed,entered
by ear or from a music score
then easily saved for play back
in Basic and other programs.

Differing instrument sounds can
also be constructed and saved. I
have updated Flexipage to easily
use Sound-Machined sounds and,
when I have obtained Sam
Computers' agreement, will
include this, with some demos,
on future sales and updates.


I am now looking forward to mags
such as yours including melodies
and differing instrument sounds
as "MM Clips" so we can share
and admire each others' efforts.


If you don't have a full review
in hand then telephone and I'll
be pleased to do one.

        SPECTRUM +3 SALES
With regard to the outboard item
from a member requiring a Spect-
rum +3 they can be purchased
"new" for `75 from Graeme Scarr,
12 St.Hildas Road, Old Trafford,
Manchester, Manchester M16 9PQ.
tel.0831-513996. He told me at
the January Birmingham show that
he buys the Spanish version and
converts them back to British!

Keep up the good work - although
I subscribe to your rivals: Sam
Supplement and Enceladus, both
of which often give you a good
run for the best - I always look
forward to your monthly disk.

         Yours Sincerely
          David Wornham

Brian Cavers to David Wornham

After getting your letter I have
ordered a copy of SOUND MACHINE
from SAMCo and hopefully we can
get some music together to put
in OUTLET.I've always been a bit
disappointed that very little
music is contributed but I am
sure it is because few people
can both understand music and
program it into SAM and those
few must think nobody else would
be interested in their efforts!
Not so! - Send 'em in!

The next version of OUTWRITE is
definitely having optional DIR's
plus variable margins as well as
many other improvements!
                        - Brian.

However, the SAM Coupe and most Spectrum printer interfaces have two"modes" of sending this data: as pure code or in "expanded" form. In this expanded form many of the codes are stopped by the computer and instead, a keyword is sent. This is for printing a BASIC listing etc. To switch the printer to do things like BOLD printing or ITALICS you need to send "control" codes. To do this you need first to make sure your computer is in the "pure code" mode as follows...

To send control codes, first:

OPEN #3;"B"          SAM COUPE, OPUS,MDRIVE

POKE @6,1            DISCIPLE/+D

FORMAT LPRINT "U"    +3

COPY: REM CHR$ 0     KEMPSTON E

After, use LPRINT to send codes. For example, to send code 65 you LPRINT CHR$ 65. Codes between 32 and 127 also have an "ASCII" equivalent so you can use that instead if you know it. To find it just enter,e.g.,PRINT CHR$ 65 and you will see a capital A on your computer screen so you can use LPRINT "A" instead of the LPRINT CHR$ 65 if you want!

I mention that because you may wonder what the printer manual means when it's got ESC &. This means the code for ESC (which is 27) and "&" (code 38) so that could be sent to the printer with either...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 38;  or...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;"&";

...it means the same. If you enter PRINT CHR$ 38 you will see a "&" on your screen.If you enter PRINT CODE "&" you will see 38 printed on your screen.Get it? Under the heading ESC & in your list next to DEC you will see it starts 27 38 0 plus other things so enter...

10 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"&";CHR$ 0; (tells printer,font is coming)

20 LPRINT CHR$ 32; (first character. - the SPACE character. This is n1 in your list)

30 LPRINT CHR$ 127; (last character, the copyright sign. This is n2 in your list)

40 LPRINT CHR$ 0; (left gap width before character. This is d1)

50 LPRINT CHR$ 16; (character pattern width. d2)

60 LPRINT CHR$ 4; (right gap width. d3)

You can try different numbers in lines 40 to 60 but they must not exceed the max values in your list. You may need to experiment and I am assuming the fonts you have are 16 dots wide (line 50) so you may need to adjust that. They could be 8 or 24 dots wide for all I know! Send me one of your fonts if you have trouble here so I can examine it.

Make sure you include all the semi-colons (;) in the above as I think you may get a linefeed when you don't want one!

Following the above,your printer should be awaiting the actual font data ("data" in your list) and this is done thus...

You must first load the font in your computer's memory. Any free area will do but let's use say, 32768. To load it and send it to your printer you need to know the length of the font code. On SAM, Disciple and +D you can get this using DIR 1. The length is the number on the far right of the filename. Other users will need a header reader if they do not know the length. Suppose the length is'L'.Add to the program:

70 LOAD "FONTNAME" CODE 32768

80 LPRINT MEM$(32768 TO 32767+L)

or... FOR N=32768 TO 32767+L: LPRINT CHR$ PEEK N; : NEXT N (Spectrum)

Obviously, you can add 32767 to the length and put the sum where I have put 32767+L.

Next you must add the number of characters which is 96. Line 120 is to end sending codes ready to send ordinary text.

После выполнения вышеуказанного
ваш принтер должен ожидать факти-
ческие данные шрифта («data» в ва-
шем списке), и это делается так...

Сначала вы должны загрузить шрифт
в память компьютера. Подойдет лю-
бая свободная область, скажем,
32768. Чтобы загрузить его и от-
править на принтер, вам нужно знать
длину кода шрифта. На SAM, Disciple
и +D вы можете получить это, ис-
пользуя DIR 1. Длина — это число
далеко справа от имени файла.
Другим пользователям понадобится
программа для чтения заголовка,
если они не знают длину. Предпо-
ложим, длина равна 'L'. Добавьте в
программу:

70 LOAD "FONTNAME" CODE 32768

80 LPRINT MEM$(32768 TO 32767+L)
                         (SAM)
или...
   FOR N=32768 TO 32767+L:
   LPRINT CHR$ PEEK N; : NEXT N
                      (Spectrum)

Очевидно, вы можете добавить 32767
к длине и поместить сумму там, где
я поставил 32767+L.

Требуется 24-битный шрифт, так что
я просто не знаю, подходят ли име-
ющиеся у вас шрифты. Дайте знать.

Затем вы должны добавить количество
символов, которое равно 96. Это тот
кусок в конце, который говорит:
n2-n1+1, и вы получаете его из 127
(последний символ в шрифте — знак
копирайта) МИНУС 32 (символ про-
бела) ПЛЮС 1. Если вы отправляете
только несколько символов, вы дол-
жны изменить это вместе с числами
в строках 20 и 30.

Наконец, СОХРАНИТЕ (SAVE) програм-
му, чтобы вы могли использовать ее
снова или изменить, если есть
ошибка!

Сохранив ее, вы можете теперь ЗА-
ПУСТИТЬ (RUN) программу, и шрифт
должен загрузиться. Когда вы захо-
тите использовать новый шрифт, вы
должны использовать...

110 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"%";CHR$ 1;

120 CLOSE #3: OPEN #3;"T"

       +D используйте POKE @6,0)

130 LPRINT "MESSAGE..."

Строка 120 предназначена для пре-
кращения отправки кодов, чтобы
можно было отправить обычный
текст.

ственный шрифт принтера, вам нужно
использовать...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;"%";CHR$ 0;

#3;"B" перед отправкой кодов (если

жалуйста, дайте мне знать и, жела-

Вставьте музыкальную кассету в магнитофон и включите воспроизведение. Просуньте острый конец отвертки в крошечное отверстие! Пошевелите им, пока не почувствуете, что попали в крошечный винт внутри. Она идеально подходит для немузыкальных людей, чтобы научиться написанию музыки, и для тех, кто уже обладает музыкальными знаниями, чтобы с легкостью использовать отличный 6-канальный звуковой чип Sam.

Мелодии можно сочинять, вводить на слух или по партитуре, а затем легко сохранять для воспроизведения в Basic и других программах.

Различные звуки инструментов также можно создавать и сохранять. Я обновил Flexipage, чтобы легко использовать звуки Sound-Machine, и, когда получу согласие Sam Computers, включу это с некоторыми демо-версиями в будущие продажи и обновления.

Теперь я с нетерпением жду, когда такие журналы, как ваш, будут включать мелодии и различные звуки инструментов в качестве "MM Clips", чтобы мы могли делиться и восхищаться усилиями друг друга.
